title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E443 (Novi Comm. Petrop. XVII, published 1773) treats the transverse vibrations of a uniform elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam) under each of the standard pairs of end conditions. The previous page finishes Problem I, the free–free bar. There the frequency equation reduces to cos ζ cosh ζ = 1, with fundamental root ζ ≈ 4.73002. This page ends that problem by noting that the higher roots ζ ≈ 5ρ−ω, 7ρ+ω, … give the same higher modes found earlier. In Euler's notation ρ is a right angle, so ρ = π/2. This page then opens Problem II (§XXIV): a lamina free at end A and pinned at end B on a peg, so that it can turn freely about it.

Modern reconstruction:
- Separation of variables gives y(x,t) = cos(θ²t) · Y(x), with Y = A cos u + B sin u + C eᵘ + D e⁻ᵘ and u = θx/b. Here b is the length constant combining stiffness Kc² and mass, and θ⁴/b⁴ is the eigenvalue of Y'''' = (θ/b)⁴ Y.
- At the free end (x = 0, called E in the text) both the bending moment and the shear vanish, Y''(0) = Y'''(0) = 0.
- Y''(0) = 0 gives −A + C + D = 0, so A = C + D.
- Y'''(0) = 0 gives −B + C − D = 0, so B = C − D.
- Euler then writes the resultant of the elementary inertial loads on the arc EY, ∫p dx = −Kc² Y''' (shear force). Its explicit form is −Kc²(θ³/b³) cos θ²t (A sin u − B cos u + C eᵘ − D e⁻ᵘ).
- He writes their moment about Y as +Kc²(θ²/b²) cos θ²t (A cos u + B sin u − C eᵘ − D e⁻ᵘ), which is −Kc² Y'' (bending moment).
- Both expressions are to be evaluated at x = a. The shear at a must balance the reaction G of the peg; this is computed on the next page.
- The next page imposes Y''(a) = 0 (no moment at a pin) and Y(a) = 0. This gives A cos ζ + B sin ζ = 0 and C e^ζ + D e^{−ζ} = 0, with ζ = θa/b. The result is the free–pinned frequency equation tan ζ = tanh ζ, equivalently e^{2ζ} = tan(π/4 + ζ), with roots ζ ≈ 3.9266, 7.0686, …

This page itself is the routine set-up of the boundary-value problem. It uses Euler's force/moment formulation (shear and moment as integrals of the inertial loads) rather than stating derivative boundary conditions directly.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The free-end conditions A = C + D and B = C − D, and the signs of the shear and moment expressions, are consistent with Y'' and Y''' of the given solution under Euler's sign convention.
Notational inconsistency only: the free end is called A in the problem statement but E in the solution. The letters A and B also serve both as end-points and as integration constants.

ideas.what: Free-end conditions written as vanishing shear and vanishing bending moment, i.e. Y''(0) = Y'''(0) = 0
ideas.modern_name: free boundary conditions for a beam
ideas.where_published: E443 Problem I (previous pages) and earlier Euler beam papers

ideas.what: Shear and moment obtained as the integral and first moment of the distributed inertial loads; the pin reaction G is obtained from equilibrium of the shear

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard setup page in E443. E443's treatment of all the end-condition cases, including free–pinned with tan ζ = tanh ζ, is well documented by Truesdell and in the Opera omnia commentary. Nothing here is uncredited or unfinished.
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image. Note that the shear-force formula's prefactor is printed as Kcc·θ³/b³ (the image shows 'θ³/b³') and the moment's prefactor as Kcc·θθ/bb; both are correctly rendered.
'vt ante' and 'conſtituebant' are read correctly; the long-s forms are preserved.
